source_checks.finding: Applies To line reads 'Windows 10 Windows 11'. The page says 'Some apps can't be uninstalled from the Settings app right now. For help uninstalling these apps, follow the instructions to uninstall from Control Panel.' The Control Panel steps are: enter Control Panel in search on the taskbar and select it; select Programs > Programs and Features; press and hold (or right-click) the program and select Uninstall or Uninstall/Change. The page says 'Note that some apps and programs are built into Windows and can't be uninstalled.' That sentence does not apply to an app the user installed.

required_actions.action: Recognize that the More menu has no Uninstall choice for a user-installed app, so the Settings method is not available
Use the Control Panel method: open Control Panel from the taskbar search, select Programs > Programs and Features, right-click or press and hold the app, then select Uninstall or Uninstall/Change

findings: Target first line: 'Apps built into Windows can't be uninstalled, so you may not see an Uninstall option for them.' The user said the app was installed by them, so this distractor sentence does not apply and suggests the app may be built in.
Target step 1 ('If the app was installed by you and still has no Uninstall option, the Microsoft page says...') is a statement, not an action.

Target step 2 only points to the 'Uninstall from Control Panel' section. The critical next action, uninstalling through Control Panel, is not given, even though the page gives the steps and the user is stuck at exactly the case the page says needs Control Panel.
correction_required: Delete the first target line about apps built into Windows. Replace the two numbered steps with the page's Control Panel method, for example: 1. Search the taskbar for Control Panel and select it. 2. Select Programs, then Programs and Features. 3. Press and hold (or right-click) the app, then select Uninstall or Uninstall/Change. Optionally add one line before the steps: 'Some apps can't be uninstalled from the Settings app right now, so use Control Panel instead.' Keep the statement in plain words and do not restate the Settings path.
